247109407_f5b6e106.text: The PVT is composed of neurons that provide dense projections via highly collateralized axons to the shell of the nucleus accumbens (NAcSh), dorsolateral bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BSTDL), lateral subregion of the central nucleus of the amygdala (CeL) (Moga et al., 1995)(Li et al., 2008)(Parsons et al., 2007)(Dong et al., 2017)(Vertes et al., 2008)(Li et al., 2021)) through which the PVT has been shown to regulate different behaviors (Choi et al., 2019)(Penzo et al., 2015)(Padilla-Coreano et al., 2011)(Do-Monte et al., 2017)(Lafferty et al., 2020)(Engelke et al., 2021)(Dong et al., 2020)(Pliota et al., 2018). Afferents from the prefrontal cortex, hypothalamus and the brainstem (Li and Kirouac 2012) are processed by PVT neurons that form a highly divergent efferent projection system to the forebrain (Li et al. 2021).
